## 1. The woman who undid her yarn  (`#the-woman-and-her-yarn`)

Cited ayat: 16:92

> **16:92** وَلَا تَكُونُوا۟ كَٱلَّتِى نَقَضَتْ غَزْلَهَا مِنۢ بَعْدِ قُوَّةٍ أَنكَٰثًا تَتَّخِذُونَ أَيْمَٰنَكُمْ دَخَلًۢا بَيْنَكُمْ أَن تَكُونَ أُمَّةٌ هِىَ أَرْبَىٰ مِنْ أُمَّةٍ إِنَّمَا يَبْلُوكُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِهِۦ وَلَيُبَيِّنَنَّ لَكُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ مَا كُنتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ

### Claims

**c1** (16:92): The ayah says not to be like her who undid her yarn into undone strands after it was made strong, taking your oaths as a means of deceit among you because one community is greater than another community.

**c2** (16:92): God only tests you by it, and on the day of resurrection He will make clear to you that over which you used to differ.

### One-minute summary

The ayah says not to be like her who undid her yarn after it was made strong, taking oaths as a means of deceit among you [c1]. It adds that God only tests you by it and will make clear on the day of resurrection that over which you used to differ [c2].

### Complete story

The ayah says not to be like her who undid her yarn into undone strands after it was made strong [c1]. It goes on that they take their oaths as a means of deceit among them because one community is greater than another community [c1]. It adds that God only tests you by it, and that on the day of resurrection He will make clear to you that over which you used to differ [c2].

### Deep study

The ayah does not use the word for a similitude here [c1]. It gives a comparison by telling the listeners not to be like the woman, and it ties the picture to taking oaths as a means of deceit [c1]. The test and the clearing up of differences are stated in the later part [c2].

### Kids mode

The ayah says not to be like her who undid her yarn after it was made strong [c1]. It says that God only tests you by it [c2].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the picture of undone strands is joined in the ayah with taking oaths as a means of deceit [c1]. Another reading is that the ayah ends by pointing to the day of resurrection, when God will make clear what they differed over [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who the woman was, where she lived or when; no person is named.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later sources name the woman and tell an account about her; this draft does not repeat or vouch for it.
- Not established: what it refers to in 'God only tests you by it'; the pronoun is read as pointing to the picture, to the oaths or to one community being greater than another.
- The ayah does not use the word mathal. That this item is grouped with the parables is the platform's classification, not the text's; the ayah gives a comparison with 'not to be like'.
- The word ankathan (undone strands) and the clause one community is greater than another (arba min ummatin) are read in more than one way; this draft keeps the wording general.
